questions.q: What does the --single-transaction flag do when used with mysqldump, per this lesson?
options: Starts the dump inside one consistent InnoDB snapshot transaction, without locking tables
Locks every table for the duration of the dump
Splits the dump into multiple separate SQL files
Disables InnoDB and forces MyISAM for the dump
questions.explain: --single-transaction uses InnoDB's MVCC-based snapshot to get a consistent dump without blocking reads or writes.

questions.q: Why is --single-transaction risky to skip against a busy production InnoDB server, per this lesson?
options: Without it, tables can be dumped at different moments in time, producing an internally inconsistent backup
Without it, mysqldump refuses to run at all
Without it, only schema is backed up, never data
Without it, the backup file cannot be compressed
questions.explain: As mysqldump walks table by table, ongoing writes without a consistent snapshot can leave different tables reflecting different points in time.

questions.q: What is the real difference between --all-databases and --databases db1 db2, per this lesson?
options: --databases (plural, named) includes CREATE DATABASE statements for the listed databases, unlike a single unnamed database dump
--all-databases only backs up the mysql system schema
--databases can only be used with MyISAM tables
They are functionally identical in every way
questions.explain: The plural --databases flag with named databases includes CREATE DATABASE statements, which a single-database dump does not.

questions.q: How is a mysqldump backup restored, per this lesson?
options: By feeding the SQL dump file back through the mysql client — there is no separate restore command
By running a dedicated mysqldump-restore utility
By using RESTORE DATABASE, the same as SQL Server
Restoring a mysqldump backup is not possible
questions.explain: Restoring a logical backup means replaying the SQL file, e.g. `mysql -u root -p < backup.sql`.

questions.q: Does --single-transaction help MyISAM tables the same way it helps InnoDB tables?
options: No — MyISAM has no transaction support, so it still needs locking to be consistent
Yes — it works identically for all storage engines
Yes, but only for tables under 1 GB
No — --single-transaction actually corrupts MyISAM tables
questions.explain: --single-transaction relies on MVCC snapshot behavior, which MyISAM doesn't have; MyISAM still requires locking for a consistent dump.
